H.R. 8476 IS A POOR SUBSTITUTE FOR ACTUAL CIVIL RIGHTS ENFORCEMENT
Finally, consideration of H.R. 8476 cannot be separated from the actions of the Administration, championed by this Majority, to tear down the Department's Office for Civil Rights. OCR is the express office charged in statute with enforcing Title VI education cases.\18\ OCR was one of the offices that lost the most employees in number and percentage as a result of the Department's reduction-in-force in 2025.\19\ The U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) documented how the Department paid OCR employees as much as $38 million to not work last year,\20\ and the Senate HELP Committee reported that in 2025, OCR had lowest rate of resolved cases in over a decade.\21\ The same Chairman that called up H.R. 8476 for consideration recently championed the interagency agreement that sent the majority of OCR's investigatory work to the Department of Justice.\22\ It remains puzzling that this majority purports to champion civil rights enforcement while simultaneously supporting the destruction of the office charged with enforcing educational civil rights.

DEMOCRATIC AMENDMENTS OFFERED DURING MARKUP OF H.R. 8476
Committee Democrats offered no amendments during the consideration of H.R. 8476.
CONCLUSION
H.R. 8476 takes an issue of legal complexity, determining if religious discrimination is also actionable as Title VI shared ancestry and national origin discrimination, and makes it even more complicated. It elevates the protection of only one religious group from discrimination over all others, and attempts to incorporate only antisemitism into Title VI, although not technically doing so. Unsettlingly, this bill includes an unnecessary definition of antisemitism that attempts to chill protected speech and may not survive First Amendment analysis.
For the reasons stated above, the majority of Committee Democrats opposed H.R. 8476 when the Committee on Education and Workforce considered it on June 25, 2026. We urge the House of Representatives to do the same.
Robert C. ``Bobby'' Scott,
Ranking Member.
Suzanne Bonamici,
Mark DeSaulnier,
Adelita Grijalva,
Members of Congress.
